anti_overlap: Does not assess mutex correctness or concurrency patterns (fd-industrial-process-control covers thread-safe accumulation), wire format JSON compatibility (fd-localization-engineering covers cross-runtime serialization), or the mirroring instruction generation text (not covered in this batch). Focuses exclusively on feature extraction fidelity, classification correctness, and EMA numeric parity.
decision_lens: A ported behavioral scoring model is correct only when: (1) every feature extracted from a raw input string is bit-for-bit identical between the source and target runtime on the same input; (2) every segment classification (the equivalent of a risk tier) assigned to an input is label-identical, not merely 'similar', between source and target; (3) the rolling score after N inputs is within machine epsilon of the source runtime's output given the same input sequence. Any port that validates only aggregate statistics ('mean segment accuracy = 98%') rather than per-input label agreement is not a correctness validation — it is a sampling exercise that will miss the tail cases that matter most.
distance_rationale: Credit risk modelers have formalized exactly the class of correctness problems that arise when a behavioral feature extraction and classification model is ported across language runtimes — regex dialect divergence, floating-point accumulation mismatch, and categorical label drift — but in a regulatory context where a scoring error has fair lending consequences, producing per-input parity validation disciplines that software engineers porting style systems rarely apply.
expected_isomorphisms: ComputeObservables corresponds to the feature extraction layer of a behavioral scorecard — a deterministic function that maps a raw text input to a fixed vector of numeric and categorical features that must be bit-reproducible across runtimes; ClassifyMode corresponds to segment assignment in a risk model — a weighted classification that must produce label-identical output on the same input regardless of which runtime executes it.
focus: Feature extraction fidelity, segment classification stability, and score accumulation correctness in behavioral scoring systems ported across language runtimes
name: fd-credit-scoring-feature-parity
persona: A senior credit risk modeler who has owned three Python-to-JVM scoring engine migrations at consumer lenders, each requiring that FICO-adjacent behavioral features extracted from raw text (payment dispute notes, call transcripts) produce numerically identical segment classifications and rolling score updates in the new runtime. Has encountered every class of regex dialect divergence, floating-point accumulation mismatch, and categorical label drift that arises when a production scoring model is re-implemented in a different language without exhaustive golden-set validation.
review_areas: Python-to-Go regex dialect divergence in observable extraction: Go's regexp package uses RE2 semantics (no backtracking, no lookahead/lookbehind), while Python's re module supports lookahead and lookaround assertions — any pattern in style.py:39-92 that uses (?=...) or (?<=...) will silently compile in Python but fail or behave differently in Go's RE2; each pattern must be audited for RE2 compatibility before claiming parity

Unicode category matching divergence: Python's \w in re matches Unicode word characters by default (including accented letters, CJK, Arabic) but Go's regexp \w matches only ASCII word characters — emoji detection, capitalization ratio, and vocabulary token extraction for non-ASCII conversations will produce different observables between Python and Go unless the patterns are explicitly updated to use Unicode character classes

Weighted mode classification tie-breaking: ClassifyMode applies weight-3 patterns (emotional), weight-2 (analytical), and weight-1 (others) — when two modes score identically, the Python dict iteration order (3.7+ insertion-ordered) determines the winner, while Go's map iteration is randomized; tie-breaking must be made explicit (e.g., prefer by mode priority order) rather than relying on source language map ordering

EMA transition boundary at N=5: the alpha formula switches from 1/(n+1) to 0.3 at n>=5; a port that applies the switch at n>5 or n>=4 will produce divergent per-mode profiles for the critical 4th and 5th messages, where the fingerprint is first becoming reliable; verify the boundary condition is tested with a golden fixture at exactly n=4, n=5, and n=6

Vocabulary counter semantics vs EMA fields: vocabulary counters (word lists) use raw increment while numeric fields (avg_words, capitalization ratio) use EMA — if the Go port accidentally applies EMA to vocabulary counters or raw increment to EMA fields, the per-mode profile will diverge silently; the JSON field names matching Python do not guarantee the update logic is correct

Golden-file test coverage of all 7 mode classifiers: a parity test suite must exercise inputs that score highest in each of the 7 modes with known observable outputs and known mode classifications; testing only emotional and general modes leaves 5 classifiers unvalidated against the Python reference

severity_examples.condition: Emotional mode is never triggered for any input in the Go port because the weight-3 patterns produce zero matches; the mode classifier defaults to general for all emotional messages; the fingerprint never accumulates an emotional profile; BuildMirroring returns instructions calibrated for general conversation for users in distress, producing responses that are tonally mismatched to the user's state — the failure is invisible in unit tests that do not compare Go output against Python reference
severity_examples.scenario: Python lookahead assertion in emotional mode pattern compiles silently in re but is unsupported in Go regexp; Go falls back to empty match

severity_examples.condition: For a user's 5th message, the Python port applies alpha=0.3 while the Go port applies alpha=1/6=0.167; the avg_words field diverges by approximately 13% of the delta between the prior EMA and the new observation; after 20 messages the divergence compounds; BuildMirroring generates different word-count thresholds between Python Auraken and Go Skaffen for the same user's conversation history, causing inconsistent mirroring instructions during the concurrent operation window
severity_examples.scenario: EMA boundary condition applied at n>5 instead of n>=5 in Go port

severity_examples.condition: For inputs that score equally on emotional and playful modes (common in casual affectionate messages), the Python port consistently returns emotional (because emotional patterns are inserted first in the Python dict) while the Go port returns either emotional or playful non-deterministically depending on map iteration seed; the per-mode fingerprint accumulates observations under different modes between runtimes, causing the two systems to develop divergent behavioral profiles for the same user over time
severity_examples.scenario: Tie-breaking in ClassifyMode relies on Go map iteration order rather than explicit priority

source_domain: Consumer credit risk modeling, behavioral scoring engine migration, Python-to-JVM feature extraction parity, FICO-adjacent segment classification
success_hints: A golden-fixture test feeds 50 pre-recorded messages from real conversations through both Python style.py and the Go package, comparing ComputeObservables JSON output field-by-field and ClassifyMode return value per message — any divergence fails the build before merge. The regex patterns are annotated with their RE2 compatibility status, and any Python-only construct is replaced with an RE2-equivalent that produces identical matches on the test corpus. The EMA boundary is tested with an explicit table-driven test at n=0,1,2,3,4,5,6 with known alpha values.
task_context: Review ComputeObservables, ClassifyMode, and the EMA update logic in the Go port of style.py. Focus on regex dialect compatibility (RE2 vs Python re), Unicode matching divergence, mode classification tie-breaking determinism, EMA boundary conditions, vocabulary counter vs EMA field update logic, and golden-file parity test coverage. Do not review database integration, mirroring instruction text quality, or Skaffen agent wiring.
